title: Doula Services Are Covered by Insurance in California — Here's What's Covered and What's Not
body_markdown:
If you're pregnant or postpartum in California, you might be surprised to learn that doula care is **covered** by all Medi-Cal plans, **and by a growing number of** private insurance plans, **including** Kaiser Permanente and Health Net.


This is a major win for birthing people and families seeking emotional, physical, and informational support during a time that's often joyful but also overwhelming and uncertain.


Here, we break down **what doula services are, which plans cover them, and what's included.**


## **What Is a Doula — and Why Does Their Support Matter?**


A **doula** is a trained, nonmedical professional who supports you during the perinatal period — before, during, and after birth.


Doulas offer hands-on comfort during labor, help you understand your options, develop a birth plan, and provide emotional and practical support during postpartum recovery.


Many people **assume** a doula's **role is** mainly in the delivery room **during** active labor. While doulas **play** a major role during labor and delivery, their **support is** just as vital in the months leading up to your due date and **in** the months after delivery. **Some doulas exclusively provide postpartum support, helping the birthing person and new infant through the "fourth trimester," as the birthing person recovers from delivery and adjusts to new parenthood.**


Research shows that continuous **doula** support is linked to:


- Lower rates of C-sections and epidural use
- Shorter labors
- Reduced rates of premature and low-birthweight births
- Improved breastfeeding outcomes
- Greater birth satisfaction and reduced anxiety during labor


In short: doulas improve health outcomes — and the experience of pregnancy, birth, and new parenthood.


## **Does Medi-Cal Cover Doula Services in California?**


**Yes.** As of January 2023, Medi-Cal **covers** doula services as a **benefit** for members who are pregnant or have been pregnant **within** the past 12 months. You **don't** need a referral **; a standing statewide recommendation from DHCS' Medical Director applies automatically, with no paperwork required.**


Coverage applies whether you're **enrolled in** a **Medi-Cal Managed Care Plan (MCP)** , like Health Net or Kaiser Permanente, or **in** **fee-for-service Medi-Cal** ( **sometimes** called "straight Medi-Cal"). The same **benefits** apply in both systems.


‍


## **Does Kaiser Permanente Cover a Doula?**


**Yes. Loula doulas are credentialed directly with Kaiser Permanente — for both Medi-Cal and commercial plans — so you don't need to worry about whether your doula is "in-network."**


**If you have Kaiser through Medi-Cal Managed Care, coverage follows the standard visit structure: an initial visit, ongoing perinatal visits, labor and birth support, and postpartum care. If you have Kaiser through a commercial or private plan, a Loula doula is already contracted with Kaiser on your behalf, so the same coverage applies.**


‍


## **Does Health Net Cover a Doula?**


**Yes. Health Net is one of Loula's core health plan partners, covering doula services under the standard visit structure — no referral needed.**


‍


## **Does Anthem Blue Cross Cover a Doula?**


**Loula is in-network with Anthem Blue Cross's Medi-Cal plan in select counties. Anthem commercial plans aren't currently covered through Loula.**[Check your coverage](https://joinloula.com/connect) **to confirm availability in your county.**


## **What Doula Services Are Covered?**


**Most insurance plans, including private plans that offer the benefit, follow** the DHCS Medi-Cal visit structure **:**


- 1 initial 90-minute visit
- 8 perinatal visits (prenatal or postpartum)
- Labor and birth support **, including support during miscarriage or abortion**
- 2 extended postpartum visits, up to 3 **hours** each
- **Up to 9 additional postpartum visits with a second provider's written recommendation**


All services can be provided in person or virtually, including by phone, **with** no location restrictions. Even if your pregnancy ends in miscarriage, stillbirth, or abortion, you're still entitled to doula support for up to one year postpartum.


‍


## **How Many Doula Visits Does Insurance Cover?**


**Under the standard Medi-Cal structure that most plans follow, you're covered for 12 total visits: 1 initial visit, 8 perinatal visits, labor and birth support, and 2 extended postpartum visits, with the option for up to 9 more postpartum visits if a second provider recommends it in writing.**


‍


## **Who's Eligible for Insurance-Covered Doula Care?**


You **'re** eligible if you are **currently** pregnant, or were **pregnant within the past year** . You **don't** need a new recommendation unless you're requesting the extended **9** additional postpartum visits. You **can** also start doula care **during** the postpartum period only, even if you didn't receive prenatal support **— and you remain eligible even if the pregnancy didn't end in a live birth.**


‍


## **Is Doula Care Covered After a Miscarriage or Stillbirth?**


**Yes. You're entitled to doula support for up to one year postpartum, regardless of whether your pregnancy ended in a live birth, miscarriage, stillbirth, or abortion.**


## **What Doula Services Are *Not* Covered by Insurance?**


**Insurance generally covers non-medical, holistic support centered on your needs, choices, and well-being — including:**


- Creating a birth plan
- Education and guidance throughout your pregnancy and postpartum journey
- Help navigating the healthcare system, like finding providers **and understanding** your options
- Emotional and physical support during labor and birth, including for miscarriage or abortion
- **Research-grounded education on childbirth, postpartum recovery, and newborn care**
- Support with breastfeeding or chestfeeding, including **positioning and latch**
- Referrals to community resources like parenting groups, mental health support, **and housing help**


The following services, while often offered by doulas, are **not reimbursable through insurance** :


- Belly binding (including traditional or ceremonial practices)
- Birthing ceremonies (such as "sealing" or "closing the bones")
- Group classes on babywearing
- Massage, **for** the birthing person or infant
- Photography or videography
- Placenta encapsulation
- Shopping or errands
- Vaginal steaming
- Yoga sessions


Doulas can still provide these services outside of insurance in two ways:


- **Pro bono** — **the doula offers the service at no cost and bills insurance only for covered services.**
- **For a fee** — **the doula charges a separate rate they set themselves, and must give you the option to opt in or out.**


Doulas are not medical professionals. **Even if they hold additional licenses, when acting as a doula they do not diagnose medical conditions, provide medical advice, or perform clinical assessments, physical exams, or medical procedures.**


## **What This Means for You**


Doula services are **more** accessible than ever in California, **with** coverage through all Medi-Cal plans and **growing** support from major private insurers like Kaiser Permanente and Health Net.. **That** means emotional, physical, and practical support during pregnancy, birth, and postpartum can be available **without** added financial stress.


Whether you're navigating pregnancy for the first time or welcoming a new addition, having a doula by your side can improve both your health outcomes and your overall experience **— from** personalized guidance and birth planning to hands-on comfort during labor and compassionate postpartum care **, even in cases of miscarriage, stillbirth, or abortion.**


If you're covered by Medi-Cal or a private plan that includes doula benefits,[check your coverage](https://joinloula.com/connect) **to see what's available to you, or reach out to a Loula doula directly.**


With insurance coverage expanding, doula care in California is becoming a right, not a luxury.


‍
